t: #2710 Remove Trailing Zeros From a String
o: Strip trailing '0' characters from a numeric string, keeping at least the leading portion (input has no leading zeros and represents a positive integer, so the result is never empty). "51230100" → "512301"; "123" unchanged.
k: Scan from the end past zeros; slice up to the last non-zero digit.
Language built-ins (rstrip/regex/find_last_not_of) do this in one line.

a.i: Move an index left while characters are '0', then return the prefix ending at that index. Since num is a positive integer without leading zeros, at least one non-zero digit exists.
s: Start i at the last index.
a.t: O(n) worst case (all but one digit zero)

a.i: Every target language offers a one-call trim: Python rstrip('0'), Java/JS regex '0+$', C++ find_last_not_of. Same complexity, less code.

w: Trivial either way; mention rstrip in an interview for fluency. Pitfall: none really — just don't convert to an integer (length up to 1000 would overflow fixed-width types). Follow-up: also strip leading zeros, or handle decimals.
